## Installing

phpolars needs PHP 8.3, 8.4, or 8.5 (non-thread-safe) on Linux or macOS. Install it with [PIE](https://github.com/php/pie):

```sh
pie install phpstats/phpolars
```

On Linux with glibc (x86_64 or arm64), PIE installs the prebuilt binary for the PHP version from the GitHub release. Elsewhere it builds from source, which needs a stable Rust toolchain and libclang and takes several minutes. See [Deployment](deployment.qmd).

From a checkout:

```sh
PHP=$(which php) PHP_CONFIG=$(which php-config) cargo build --profile dist
php -d extension=$PWD/target/dist/libphp_polars.so script.php   # .dylib on macOS
```

On macOS with Homebrew, also set `LIBCLANG_PATH=$(brew --prefix llvm)/lib`. When several PHP versions are installed, point `PHP` and `PHP_CONFIG` at the PHP you will load the extension into, because the build uses that PHP's headers.

## Imports

Classes live in `Phpolars` and functions are namespaced, so import them:

```php
use Phpolars\{DataFrame, Series};
use function Phpolars\{col, lit, when, read_csv};
```

## A first query

{{< include examples/_select.md >}}

Strings passed where py-polars expects an expression input, such as `select()`, name columns. Use `lit()` for a string value there. In comparisons and arithmetic, strings are literals: `col('store')->ne('S1')`.

## Grouping

{{< include examples/_group-by.md >}}

`groupBy()` follows py-polars and does not keep group order unless `maintainOrder: true` is passed.
